text:
maya: heads up — noticed p99 jump on prod after yesterday's proxy rewrite. flamegraph here: https://internal.perf/fg/80808
jon: saw the alert. can you paste the top samples from pprof or a small flame snippet?
maya: flame shows large time in rust proxy writev path + chunk_splice_loop. lots of small writes clustered. attaching screenshot link: https://img.internal/fg/snippet-80808
sam: that matches what i saw in the stress harness — splay heuristic seems to be producing many tiny frames instead of coalesced chunks. small writes -> syscall overload -> tail latency.
rachel: pulling perf now. quick sample from `perf top` on a repro node:
```
writev 42%
tokenize 10%
parse_request 8%
kvcache_lookup 6%
__sys_epoll_wait 5%
```
edgebot: regression-bot: deploy 2026-03-19 "proxy-rust-chunk-splay" increased p99 latency by +15% vs baseline (observed 03/20 09:12 UTC). :warning:
jon: can we repro locally? maya: yes on the new stress harness with seq_len=32, qps=120 and concurrency=80. sam: i repro too — kernel selection takes the "small-batch" execution path which then flips kernels frequently and we lose benefits of batching.
rachel: also seeing higher KV cache evictions during the spike — likely fragmentation from many tiny requests causing hot-shard churn.
sam: short-term mitigations: revert the splay change or add a proxy-side coalescer that holds tiny frames for 1-2ms to combine writes. longer-term: tweak batching heuristic to prefer coalescing when payload < X and writev rate > Y.
jon: any perf numbers on coalescing? sam: ran microbench: coalescing small writes into <8 per writev reduced writev syscalls by ~60% and improved p99 by ~25% in the harness. throughput unchanged.
maya: can someone open a canary PR with the coalescing option gated? we need metrics on real traffic before full rollback.
rachel: i'll open PR + add dashboard chart: writev_count, epoll_wakeups, kvcache_evictions, p99. will also attach flame snapshots pre/post.
jon: i'll run kvcache profiling and kernel-selection telemetry once the canary lands.
perf-bot: SUMMARY: probable root = splay heuristic -> small-write amplification -> syscall/writev tail -> higher p99 and increased KV eviction churn. ACTIONS: 1) open canary PR with coalescing (rachel), 2) run kvcache + kernel-selection prof (jon), 3) evaluate revert if canary fails (maya).
maya: thanks — tagging @sam for the coalescer implementation. :thumbsup:
